name: EXAONE-Tabular
family: EXAONE Tabular (LG AI Research's EXAONE family; first tabular member, v1.0)
developer: LG AI Research (Moonjung Eo, Min-Kook Suh, Hye-Seung Cho, Jiwon Kim, Seoyoon Kim, Sangjun Nam, Soonyoung Lee)
paper_title: EXAONE Tabular 1.0: Technical Report - A Synthetic-Prior Foundation Model for Tabular Classification and Regression

availability.notes: Release timeline: code + classification checkpoint published 2026-07-31 (GitHub commit 'EXAONE Tabular 1.0.0', HF repo created 2026-07-31); regression checkpoint released 2026-08-06 (GitHub PR #1 'Release EXAONE-Tabular Regression', HF 'Upload regressor weight'); classifier weights republished in place on 2026-08-06; press announcement 2026-08-07; technical report on arXiv 2026-08-26 (v1, 18 pages) and added to the repos 2026-08-27. The GitHub repo is only the 'exaonetabular' inference runtime (scikit-learn-style EXAONETabularClassifier / EXAONETabularRegressor, from_pretrained downloads weights from the Hub, no token or gating). No training code, no synthetic-prior generator and no training data are released. Not on PyPI: install with pip from the git URL (Python >= 3.11, PyTorch >= 2.6, < 3). Weights: float32 safetensors; default checkpoints exaone-tabular-classifier-v1_default and exaone-tabular-regressor-v1_default plus 2 extra classifier and 7 extra regressor checkpoints (hash-suffixed) in the HF repo; files are served from the mutable 'main' revision without a sha256 pin (loads log an 'unverified' warning). CUDA GPU strongly recommended (fp16 + FlashAttention); CPU inference works in float32 but is slow.

architecture.type: Cross-Axis Summary Transformer (CAST): cell-level 2D in-context transformer that interleaves feature-axis attention within each row and support-conditioned item-axis attention within each feature at every layer, mediated by learned item-summary and feature-summary tokens
architecture.parameters_note: Classification checkpoint 20,807,866 parameters (~20.65M backbone + ~0.156M task head); regression checkpoint ~21,110,247 (same backbone + distributional quantile head with decoder hidden width 384). Sizes are the weights stored in the evaluated checkpoints.
architecture.layers: 12 CAST layers; each layer = 2 feature-axis self-attention operations (per item, over its cells + 3 item-summary tokens, preceded by cross-attention from cells to their feature-summary states) + 1 item-axis attention block (per feature, over support cells + 32 feature-summary tokens, preceded by cross-attention from cells to their item-summary states)
architecture.attention_scheme: Feature axis: self-attention within each row over [3 item-summary tokens + F cells]; item axis, per feature, over [32 feature-summary tokens + Ns support cells] with two paths - support path (self-attention jointly updating feature-summary tokens and support cells) and query path (each query cell cross-attends to the same support+summary sequence; queries never attend to each other and do not update support/summary states), so query predictions are conditionally independent given the support set and can be chunked. Scalable Softmax (SSMax) normalization per head for context-length generalization. Feed-forward expansion 4x, single shared MLP ('MLP sharing: single'). Cost per estimator: feature attention linear in items, quadratic in feature groups; item attention O(Ns^2 + Ns*Nq). Kernels: FlashAttention / memory-efficient attention dispatch, fp16 default.
architecture.checkpoints: separate classification & regression checkpoints (same backbone architecture, trained separately from scratch; no shared dual-head checkpoint)
architecture.regression_head: distributional: 999 conditional quantiles (tau_k = k/1000, k=1..999); default point estimate = quantiles sorted (to prevent crossing) then trapezoidal average over the central 99.8% of the quantile function (approximates the conditional mean); median readout optional
architecture.feature_embedding: Each feature/cell encoded independently; finite values and indicators for missing or infinite values are processed jointly by a dedicated missing-value handling step, so the model uses both observed values and missingness patterns; cell-level representations are kept throughout the network (no row compression). Classification head: two-layer MLP decoder to logits over up to 10 classes with softmax.
key_innovations: CAST: no one-time compression of rows into a fixed embedding before a separate ICL stage (unlike TabICL/TabICLv2/TabPFN-3/TabFM); feature-axis and item-axis processing are interleaved in all 12 layers so support context formed in one layer refines feature representations in later layers

Two complementary summary-token pathways: 3 item-summary tokens per row concatenated along the feature axis and 32 feature-summary tokens per feature concatenated along the support item axis, persisting across layers (vs. TabPFN-v2 style alternating attention without persistent summaries)
Support/query split in item-axis attention gives conditional independence of query rows -> query chunking and optional reuse of support-side keys/values across chunks
SSMax attention normalization; native missing-value handling with missingness indicators (no imputation required)

Compact size (~21M) reaching the TabFM (1.64B) performance regime at ~1/11 the inference cost; ECOC decomposition for >10 classes; 999-quantile distributional regression head with trimmed-mean readout
Training: Muon optimizer for matrix parameters + AdamW for the rest, WSD schedule, EMA weights

capabilities.max_classes_note: Native head supports up to 10 classes (class_capacity=10). More classes are handled automatically at inference by an Error-Correcting Output Code (ECOC) decomposition into several <=10-symbol subproblems evaluated with the same model, at proportionally higher inference cost.
capabilities.max_features_note: Classifier: the model reads at most 100 columns (feature_limit=100); wider tables are reduced automatically inside fit by attention-based feature selection (one forward pass over <=512 rows scoring columns from target-token and item-summary attention weighted by value norms; cannot be disabled). Regressor: reads up to 1024 columns (feature_limit=1024); wider tables trimmed by univariate f_regression, then 16 support-SVD components are appended per ensemble member. Inputs must be 2-D numeric NumPy arrays.
capabilities.max_samples_note: Default support_row_limit=100000 (paper Fig. 2: 'Support rows Ns <= 100k'); larger support sets are randomly subsampled before preprocessing. No documented limit on query rows (queries are chunked, query_batch_limit=1024). TabArena datasets go up to 250k training rows; for BCCO/TALENT LG capped support at 50k rows per fold.
capabilities.categorical_features: Must be ordinal-encoded to numeric codes by the caller (raw strings raise); unseen categories can be left as NaN. Test-time ensembling permutes categorical encodings. The synthetic prior includes categorical discretization.
capabilities.other: Regression outputs 999 conditional quantiles (predictive distribution; CRPS-evaluated on ScoringBench) with trimmed-mean or median point readout; targets standardized internally, NaN/inf targets rejected. Classification predict_proba. Regression ensemble members are combined with NNLS weights fitted on a 20% held-out slice of the support set (needs >= 2000 held-out rows, i.e. engages from ~10k support rows; uniform averaging below that), blended 75/25 with uniform weights. GPU memory planner with hard max_vram_bytes cap; ensemble_count, compute_dtype (float16 default, bfloat16 optional, float32 CPU-only) and seed are runtime knobs. No embeddings API, no multi-target, no text/time-series.

pretraining.synthetic_prior_summary: Five-stage SCM generator (not released): (i) sample task hyperparameters - number of rows, features, classes, graph size, component structure, mechanism families - over broad ranges subject to a per-task compute budget; (ii) sample a DAG with one or two weakly connected components via a randomized topology procedure, assign each edge one of three mechanism families (neural transformation = smooth nonlinearity, tree-based rule = piecewise threshold, identity mapping) and sample independent per-node noise (Gaussian/Poisson/uniform shown in Fig. 2); (iii) evaluate the SCM in topological order: root nodes from exogenous draws, each other node a scaled sum of per-edge mechanism outputs plus optional per-node Gaussian noise; (iv) pick a subset of nodes as observed features and one node as target, split rows into support and query (classification and regression episodes differ in target construction and sampling settings); (v) post-process: categorical discretization, nonlinear feature warping, feature-wise quantization, task-specific missingness injection, optional quality filter removing tasks that are too easy, too noisy or uninformative. No real tables used.
synthetic_prior_types: post-hoc categorical discretization, warping, quantization, missingness injection
pretraining.num_synthetic_datasets_note: Report Sec. 3: 'classification processes approximately 30 million synthetic table instances, while regression processes approximately 10 million' across the training lineage of the released models (count = table instances processed during optimization, so repeats are possible; generation is on the fly). Press coverage (Asia Business Daily 2026-08-07, IoT Tech News 2026-09-15) instead says 'trained on more than one billion synthetic tabular data examples' - unit not defined (probably rows/samples rather than tables); the two figures are not reconciled in any official source.
pretraining.real_data: none (pretrained entirely on synthetic SCM data; no real-data fine-tuning reported)
pretraining.objective: Not stated explicitly. Classification head yields softmax probabilities over <= 10 classes; regression head predicts 999 conditional quantiles - the corresponding losses (cross-entropy / quantile loss) are implied but not named in the report.
pretraining.optimizer: Muon (momentum + matrix orthogonalization) for most matrix-valued parameters (attention and feed-forward weight matrices), AdamW for all remaining parameters. Learning rates - classification: 1e-4 (AdamW) / 2e-4 (Muon); regression: 3.8e-5 (AdamW) / 2e-4 (Muon); learning rates and weight decay adjusted in later stages. Schedule: Warmup-Stable-Decay (WSD) for main training, cosine or constant LR for continuation/adaptation stages. EMA of weights with decay 0.999 (stage-specific adjustments late in classification training); EMA weights used for evaluation and release. bf16 training precision.
pretraining.training_steps: Not stated (only ~30M tables for classification and ~10M for regression processed across all stages).
pretraining.hardware: Not stated (no GPU type or count disclosed in report, README or model card).
pretraining.training_cost_note: No training compute, GPU-hours, wall-clock or cost figures are published anywhere; only the table counts above.
pretraining.curriculum: Multi-stage 'training lineage': WSD main phase followed by continuation and adaptation stages with adjusted LR/weight decay (cosine/constant schedules) and EMA; task size/structure sampled over broad ranges under a per-task compute budget. No explicit context-length or difficulty curriculum is described.

icl.context_note: support_row_limit=100000 by default (RuntimeConfig; Fig. 2 'Ns <= 100k'); adjustable via the low-level manifest (RuntimeConfig(support_row_limit=...)). Item-axis attention over the support set is quadratic in Ns, so memory grows with support size; the planner chunks members/queries/FFN tokens and can offload the support cache to fit the VRAM budget.
icl.large_dataset_strategy: Random subsampling of the support set to the row limit (100k) before preprocessing; query chunking (queries conditionally independent given the support set) with automatic choice between cached execution (support-side keys/values built once per estimator x ECOC subproblem and reused across query chunks) and uncached execution (support recomputed per chunk); estimator-axis chunking; wide tables reduced by feature selection. The report lists context compression, representative/clustering/retrieval-based context selection and adaptive support sampling as future work.
icl.test_time_ensembling: Default 8 estimators for both checkpoints (ensemble_count=8): members differ in preprocessing (raw, robust scaling, power transform, quantile transform), categorical-encoding, feature-order and class-label permutations; classification averages probabilities; regression combines members with NNLS weights (>= ~10k support rows) or uniform mean, and by default runs an additional SVD-augmented ensemble (svd_split=True, 16 SVD components) pooled with the plain one, i.e. 16 members and double the forward passes at fit and predict. Ensemble size adjustable for latency/accuracy; TabArena uses the default (no HPO search space, can_hpo=False).
icl.fine_tuning: Not supported by the released package (inference-only runtime, no training code). Custom weights of the same architecture can be loaded via from_pretrained(weights=...) or an explicit InferenceManifest, but no fine-tuning recipe is provided; in-context adaptation only.
icl.inference_notes: fit() only stores/preprocesses the support set (no gradient updates); one fit may involve E x R x n_query_chunks forward operations (E estimators, R ECOC subproblems). Default compute dtype fp16 (bf16 optional; fp32 only on CPU because part of the stack is pinned to FlashAttention). Extra passes: classification on >100 columns runs one <=512-row feature-selection pass; regression from ~10k rows runs one extra pass for NNLS weights. Peak-memory planner with max_vram_bytes hard cap (~10% safety margin); CUDA OOM is raised to the caller (no automatic retry). TabArena wrapper: refit_folds=True, sequential fold fitting, GPU required.

speed.hardware_note: Official TabArena leaderboard timings (README/report, Aug 2026 snapshot): median 5.79 s train and 0.605 s predict per 1,000 samples on TabArena's GPU pipeline (GPU type not stated in LG's docs). TabArena's 2026-09-16 rerun of all hosted foundation models on 32 spot g4-standard-48 workers (RTX PRO 6000, 96 GB) under the new timing/warm-up pipeline reduced EXAONE's median train time from 5.79 to 2.00 s per 1K rows (Elo 1737, within noise of the hosted result). Third-party snapshot in the Xiaomi-TabLDM report (Sep 2026): 9.00 s train / 2.10 s predict per 1K overall, 13.71 / 2.58 s on regression.
speed.memory_note: Attention memory grows quadratically with support rows (up to 100k) and with feature count; the runtime plans chunking (members, query rows, FFN tokens) and support-cache offload against a VRAM budget (max_vram_bytes; default = all addressable VRAM). Recommended OOM remedies: PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True, lower max_vram_bytes, lower ensemble_count, lower support_row_limit, bigger GPU. Weights ~21M params (float32 file, cast to fp16 at load).
speed.speed_claims: Report: with default single-forward-pass inference at 0.605 s per 1,000 samples EXAONE Tabular lies on the accuracy-latency Pareto front of both TabArena task types; regression reaches TabFM's accuracy regime at roughly 1/11 the inference cost (TabFM ~7.0 s per 1K samples, ~11.5x; README table: 6.985 s). Press (IoT Tech News): LG cut the time needed to respond to manufacturing model changes by 85%.
speed.inference_cost_note: No hosted API or pricing; free local inference under the non-commercial weights license. CUDA GPU strongly recommended; CPU float32 path is slow.

talent.source: EXAONE Tabular 1.0 Technical Report, Sec. 4.5 / Fig. 7 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25774)
talent.protocol_note: LG-run controlled comparison of 7 tabular foundation models (EXAONE Tabular, TabSwift, TabDPT, TabPFN-3, TabICLv2, LimiX, TabFM) using official repos/checkpoints and each model's default preprocessing; 188 of the 200 TALENT classification datasets (12 datasets with >10 classes excluded) and all 100 regression datasets; training/support set capped at 50,000 samples per fold (validation/test unchanged); ordinal encoding for models needing numeric inputs; 8 ensemble members for all models except TabFM (32). Metrics: mean test accuracy (classification) and mean R2 (regression) with 95% bootstrap CIs; no average ranks reported by LG.
talent.other: Classification mean accuracy 0.857 (2nd of 7; TabFM 0.863, TabPFN-3 0.854, TabICLv2 0.854, TabDPT 0.849, TabSwift 0.841, LimiX 0.834). Regression mean R2 0.736 (1st; TabFM 0.733, TabPFN-3 0.728, TabICLv2 0.723, TabDPT 0.715, LimiX 0.713, TabSwift 0.708). Third-party (Xiaomi-TabLDM report, arXiv 2609.03880, own protocol, 300 datasets): EXAONE-Tabular average rank 4.15 on the 100 regression datasets (3rd behind TabFM 3.72 and TabLDM 4.03; TabPFN-v3 4.88, TabICLv2 6.10), 4.96 overall (3rd; TabFM 4.23, TabLDM 4.82, TabPFN-v3 5.55) and 6.38 on binary classification (TabLDM/TabFM 5.72, TabPFN-v3 6.80).

differences_vs_predecessor: First release (v1.0) - there is no predecessor tabular model from LG; the report calls it 'LG AI Research's first tabular foundation model family'. It shares only the EXAONE brand with LG's LLM/VLM line (EXAONE 4.5, K-EXAONE) and with EXAONE Forecast (time-series model announced the same day). Architecturally it positions itself against TabPFN v2/2.5 (cell-level alternating attention, but adds persistent feature-summary tokens and item-summary tokens), TabICL/TabICLv2/TabPFN-3 (staged row-compression before ICL, which CAST avoids) and TabFM (1.64B, ~78x larger). Within v1.0: regression checkpoint added 2026-08-06 (one week after the classifier), classifier weights silently republished in place the same day, weights license 1.1-NC -> 1.2-NC in Aug 2026.
